items.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: Emily Remler, the great guitar player, came through Billings about four months before she died, so I got to hang with her a little bit.

ctx.x: Well there’s more jazz in Idaho than there is in Montana?

Well at least I thought there was. I mean I think it’s all over but it’s just where you look. And I think as long as you’re open to it and receptive to it, it will find you. And it was one of those things that even though I was living in Boise, Idaho at the time when Gene Harris was there, because of my age and the society there, it was not cool for a seventh or an eighth grader to go to the local bar to go hear jazz musicians. So I never actually got to know who Gene Harris was until after I’d moved away. But…
evening, nothing. He just felt my calluses. And I’ve never had anybody feel my callus before. And I’m like what is this? And it was like, “You need to practice more.”
